items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So Norman Granz say, we ain’t playing no segregated auditorium.

ctx.x: ’49. You would have been about 15. Pretty young. Talking to Diz about. Was he open? Was he receptive to . . . ?

I didn’t talk to him then. I talked to him later on. But I went to the concert. The concert was at the Booker Washington auditorium. Mixed concerts was forbidden. So Norman Granz say, we ain’t playing no segregated auditorium. So what he did, he brought the concert to Booker T. Washington High School auditorium, and they figured out how to segregate it anyway. That was kind of funny, in a way. Downstairs – and how I found out was sheer accident – I had a ticket for seat whatever it was, E-3 or whatever. All these…

You were talking about when you were doing your – with that band, I think that you were saying that you were doing recording. You were all contributing music. What was the music sounding like? Who were the major influences on these original compositions that you were all playing?
